subject: Mid-cycle growth: stitching additional capacity, credit mechanics, and co-term options
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@novahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com, Amit Shah <amit.shah@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity ask + co-term question

Hi Hannah,

Hope you had a good holiday — quick one from procurement: our Q1 pilot ran hotter than expected and we need to add capacity mid-cycle. We’re looking at roughly +200k monthly tokens for the remainder of our current 10-month term (ends 2026-10-31).

Two asks: can you (1) outline options for adding this capacity (commit top-up vs transient burst vs voucher) and the billing/proration impact, and (2) confirm whether we can co-term this additional capacity to our existing renewal so it’s on the same renewal date? Procurement is targeting a signed amendment within 14 days.

Attaching our Q4 usage so you can see the spike: usage_report_q4.csv (csv).

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Park
Head of AI Integrations
Nova Health


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Mid-cycle capacity ask + co-term question (Nova Health)

Ben / Priyom,

FYI from Nova Health (Lena). They need ~+200k tokens/mo for the remainder of the term and want an amendment signed within 14 days. My quick read: options are (A) committed top-up (pro-rated for remainder of term) with a small uplift discount for commit, (B) voucher/one-time prepay that smooths invoicing but doesn’t count as committed units, or (C) burst capacity (hosted) at higher overage rates.

Questions for pricing/legal: what discount can we offer for a commit that starts mid-term? Can we offer a blended rate to keep monthly invoices predictable? They also asked to co-term the top-up to the existing renewal.

Can you propose two firm options I can send today (one conservative, one aggressive) and a suggested line for the amendment (short SOW + signature)? I’ll route externally.

Thanks — Hannah
(Hannah Schmitt, Account Executive)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Mid-cycle capacity ask + co-term question (Nova Health)

Hannah / Priyom,

Quick proposal: two options we can position immediately. I attached a draft SOW to make it concrete (NovaHealth_SOW_draft.pdf).

Option 1 (Conservative, preferred for predictability):
- Add 200k tokens/month as committed top-up for the remainder of term (7 months remaining).
- Pro-rate first invoice for the partial month, then full monthly invoicing.
- 8% uplift discount on top-up units (applied to top-up only) in exchange for commit.
- Co-term: yes, amendment ties top-up to existing renewal date; no change to base contract term.

Option 2 (Flexible, quicker close):
- One-time voucher of equivalent value (prepay for 7 months of 200k).
- Voucher carries a 5% discount (prepay incentive); does not change committed units.
- If they convert voucher to commit before renewal, apply credit for amount used.

Notes and asks:
- If legal is OK, we can include a 30-day exit for the top-up if usage drops >40% vs consumption forecast (protects us).
- For an aggressive close, we can bump Option 1 discount to 10% but require a formal PO and a 12-month renewal extension.

Numbers to supply in external email: monthly sticker for top-up before discount $X = $0.018/token * 200,000 = $3,600 (example). With 8% discount => $3,312/mo. If they want 10% we go to $3,240/mo.

I’d recommend we lead with Option 1 at 8% and offer Option 2 as a fallback. Legal and billing need to confirm the pro-rate math and amendment language.

Ben
VP, Customer Success (Sales Operations)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@novahealth.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@novahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity ask + co-term question

Hi Lena / Amit — thanks for the quick heads up and the usage attachment. Apologies for the stream of internal notes below. Per Ben and our ops team, here are two options we can put in an amendment today: 

Option A (predictable commit) 
- Add 200k tokens/month as a committed top-up for the remainder of your term (7 months).
- Pro-rated charge for January (based on activation date) then monthly invoices thereafter.
- 8% discount applied to the top-up units for the remainder of term.
- Amendment will be co-term with your existing renewal date (no change to overall term length).
- Inclusion of a usage-smoothing safeguard: if actual consumption drops >40% vs forecast over any two-month window, we will review and can offer a one-time credit adjustment.

Option B (prepay voucher)
- One-time prepayment equivalent to 7 months of 200k tokens, applied as a voucher to invoices.
- 5% prepay discount.
- Voucher does not change committed units; you retain flexibility.

If you prefer a faster close we can increase offer on Option A to a 10% discount if you agree to add a 12-month renewal extension at the current committed baseline.

Next steps: if either option looks good, I can send a short amendment (SOW + signature page) and a DocuSign link. Ben attached a draft SOW for your review (shared link: https://drive.google.com/novamed/sow-v2).

Can you confirm preferred option and PO timing? Procurement mentioned a 14-day window to sign.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Amit
